translated_text: In the beginning, the High Plain of Heaven was formed, and a deity was born called Heavenly Spirit, the Master of the Center.
original_text: 天初之時、高天原成神號天之御中主神。

translated_text: Next was the High Producing Wondrous Spirit. Next was the Divine Producing Wondrous Spirit. These two deities also came into being alone.
original_text: 次高御產巢日神。次神產巢日神。此二柱神亦獨神成坐。

translated_text: Next was the Heavenly Eternal Standing Deity. Next was the Land Eternal Standing Deity. These two also came into be alone.
original_text: 次天之常立神。次國之常立神。此二柱亦獨神成坐。

translated_text: Heaven and earth were separated; heaven existed in the High Plain of Heaven, while the land floated like oil upon the waters.
original_text: 天地判而、天在高天原、地在海上浮萍之如。

translated_text: At that time, grass and reeds sprouted forth, as if floating oil upon the water, and waved gently.
original_text: 當時草芽芽立、如浮脂而、水中蠕蠕動。

translated_text: These two deities standing on the Heavenly Floating Bridge, looked down upon the land below.
original_text: 此二神如水蚊而、立天之浮橋而、指下而見其浮沼。

translated_text: The Male Who Invites and the Female Who Invites together counseled, and taking the Heavenly Jeweled Spear, thrust it down and stirred the brine.
original_text: 其美斗能男神與天之細女命、共議而、天之沼矛以指下而、畫攪其天沼矛。

translated_text: From the tip of the spear, the brine gathered and hardened to form an island, named Onogoroshima.
original_text: 其矛先從下凝成一島、淤能碁呂島と號。

translated_text: Then Amaterasu the Great Shining Deity and Takami Musubi no Mikoto gave birth together to a deity called Thought-Curator.
original_text: 於是天照大御神與高產靈命、合而生神、號八意思兼神。

translated_text: Izanagi and Izanami stood upon the Heavenly Floating Bridge, and thrusting down the Heavenly Jeweled Spear, stirred the brine.
original_text: 伊奘諾與伊奘冊立天浮橋之上、指下而指其天沼矛。

translated_text: From the tip of the spear, the brine hardened into an island; upon this land they erected the Heavenly Pillar and built an eight-fathom palace.
original_text: 其矛先自下凝成一島、即於其國、立天之御柱、巡八尋殿。

translated_text: Izanagi asked Izanami: How is your body formed?
original_text: 伊奘諾問伊奘冊曰、汝之身如何成。

translated_text: Izanami replied: My body is formed in layers, and there is one place that is not complete.
original_text: 伊奘冊答曰、吾身層成有、不完全之處一處在。

translated_text: Then the two deities mated and bore a child, the deity Awashima.
original_text: 於是二神合而生子、淡島此神。

translated_text: This deity was not fit to be enshrined, and was cast into the sea.
original_text: 此神不宜奉齋、復投棄於海。

translated_text: They again bore a child, the deity Nuna-Kaha-Hiko and the deity Nuna-Kaha-Hime.
original_text: 復生子、沼河比古神與沼河比賣神。

translated_text: Again they bore a child, the deity Yama-no-Hiko and the deity Yama-no-Hime.
original_text: 又生子、山之比古神與山之比賣神。

translated_text: Again they bore a child, the deity Kaze-no-Hiko and the deity Kaze-no-Hime.
original_text: 又生子、風之比古神與風之比賣神。

translated_text: Thus they bore the deity of trees, the deity of fields, the deity of the sea, the deity of mountains, the deity of the earth.
original_text: 如是生木之神、野之神、海之神、山之神、土之神。

translated_text: Izanagi drew his mighty sword and cut off the head of the Fire God Kagutsuchi.
original_text: 伊奘諾命拔十拳劒而、斬迦具土神之首。

translated_text: The blood from the sword splashed and gave rise to deities, called Heavenly Mars.
original_text: 其劒之血飛濺、從劒生神、號天津甕星。

translated_text: Thus, because of his burns, Izanagi ascended to the Land of Yellow Springs.
original_text: 如是因火傷而、伊奘諾命者、遂升于黄泉國矣。

translated_text: Izanagi, missing his younger sister Izanami, went searching to the Land of Yellow Springs.
original_text: 伊奘諾命思其妹伊奘冊命之故、尋至黄泉國。

translated_text: When he reached the Palace of Yomi, Izanami came out from within and said:
original_text: 至黄泉國而、其殿之前至時、伊奘冊自殿之内出迎、語而曰。

translated_text: My lord, why have you come so late? I have already eaten the food of the Yellow Land.
original_text: 吾夫君也、何來遲乎。吾既不食黄泉國之物。

translated_text: Yet since you have come to seek me, I wish to return to the land of the living. But I have made a covenant with the gods of Yomi, and you must not look inside.
original_text: 雖然汝來迎之、吾欲歸於地上。然與黄泉神相約、不可出追。

translated_text: Izanagi secretly took his left bag, lit a pine torch, and went inside to look.
original_text: 伊奘諾命竊取左之御囊、取松之明火、往入內而見。

translated_text: He saw that flies swarmed upon her body, clustering like bees.
original_text: 見其身者、蠅聚集而如蜂之集。

translated_text: Izanagi was terrified and fled from the Land of Yellow Springs.
original_text: 伊奘諾命者驚而、復還逃于黄泉國之前。

translated_text: Izanami, enraged, said: You have disgraced me; I shall kill a thousand of your people every day.
original_text: 伊奘冊命怒曰、辱吾身、吾欲日殺汝國千人。

translated_text: Izanagi replied: Then I shall give life to fifteen hundred every day.
original_text: 伊奘諾命答曰、吾則日產千五百人。

translated_text: From this, death and life began.
original_text: 自此始有死與生。

translated_text: Izanagi wished to purify himself and went to Ame-no-Ohashi-hara in Hyuga no Kuni to perform purification.
original_text: 伊奘諾命欲除穢、至筑紫日向橘小戸之阿波岐原行禊。

translated_text: He threw away his staff, threw away his garland.
original_text: 投棄其持杖、投棄其持鬘。

translated_text: He removed his robe, removed his sash, removed his shoes, removed his trousers.
original_text: 脫其衣、脫其帶、脫其鞋、脫其裳。

translated_text: He entered the river and washed his body.
original_text: 入河而洗身。

translated_text: Then, washing his left eye, he gave birth to Amaterasu, the Great Shining Deity of Heaven.
original_text: 於是左之御目洗而生天照大御神。

translated_text: Washing his right eye, he gave birth to Tsukuyomi no Mikoto.
original_text: 右之御目洗而生月讀命。

translated_text: Washing his nose, he gave birth to the Swift-Impetuous Male Deity, Susanoo.
original_text: 洗其鼻而生建速須佐之男命。

translated_text: These three deities are the most noble.
original_text: 此三柱之神者、是貴也。

translated_text: Susanoo, the Deity of the Storm, always wept for his mother in the Land of Yellow Springs.
original_text: 須佐之男命者、常哭泣其母於黄泉國。

translated_text: His crying dried up the mountains and rivers; therefore the gods commanded and banished him.
original_text: 其哭泣者山枯れ川枯れ。是以諸神勅而逐。

translated_text: Susanoo said: I wish to go where my mother is.
original_text: 須佐之男命言曰、吾欲往母在處。

translated_text: Then Amaterasu asked: Why do you come up to the High Plain?
original_text: 於是天照大御神問曰、汝何故上來乎。

translated_text: Susanoo said: I wish to leave the land of the living and go to the Land of Roots.
original_text: 須佐之男曰、吾欲離地上、往根之堅國。

translated_text: Amaterasu said: That is not good.
original_text: 天照大御神曰、然則不得善。

translated_text: Susanoo descended from Heaven and arrived in the Land of Izumo.
original_text: 須佐之男命從天上降、出雲國者乃到。

translated_text: There were an old man and an old woman, and their daughter sat weeping.
original_text: 有老夫與老媼二人、其女子一人泣居。

translated_text: Susanoo asked: Why are you weeping?
original_text: 須佐之男問曰、汝等何為泣乎。

translated_text: The old man answered: We have an eight-headed serpent that comes each year and devours our daughter.
original_text: 老夫答曰、吾等有八頭大蛇、每年來食吾女子。

translated_text: Susanoo said: I shall slay that serpent for you.
original_text: 須佐之男曰、吾為汝殺其蛇。

translated_text: He then made eight vats of sake and placed them at the eight gates where the serpent would enter.
original_text: 乃作酒八樽、置蛇入之八門。

translated_text: The serpent drank the sake, became drunk, and fell asleep.
original_text: 蛇飲酒醉而眠。

translated_text: Susanoo drew his sword and slew the serpent. From its tail emerged the Heavenly Sword Kusanagi.
original_text: 須佐之男拔劒斩蛇。其尾之中、天叢雲劒出。

translated_text: Susanoo committed many wicked deeds. Amaterasu was greatly afraid and hid herself in the Heavenly Rock Cave.
original_text: 須佐之男命行惡事多。天照大御神大に懼而、天石窟に隠れ給ふ。

translated_text: Thus, between heaven and earth, it became dark, as if the light of the sun and moon had vanished.
original_text: 是以天地之間暗くして、日月の光なきが如し。

translated_text: Then the eight million gods assembled at the head of the Heavenly River Ame no Yasukara and consulted with the Deity of Mighty Hands.
original_text: 於是八百万の神、天安河の川上に会し、天手力男神に謀る。

translated_text: They had Ame no Uzume no Mikoto perform a dance and laugh aloud.
original_text: 天鈿女命を以て舞せしめ、笑はしむ。

translated_text: Ame no Uzume stepped upon a great tub, pulled her sash down below her waist, bared her breast, and laughed aloud.
original_text: 天鈿女命、大瓮に蹈み乗りて、裳を帯の下に押垂れ、胸を露わにして、笑はしむ。

translated_text: Then Amaterasu peered slightly from the cave entrance.
original_text: 於是天照大御神、少し窓より覗き給ふ。

translated_text: The Deity of Mighty Hands pulled her out by her hand.
original_text: 天手力男神、其御手を引き出だす。

translated_text: Then Ame no Tajikara o hung a sacred rope and said: You must not go back inside.
original_text: 天太玉命、注連を張り、曰く、此より内には入り給ふなと。

translated_text: Prince Yamato Takeru was the son of Emperor Keiko.
original_text: 倭建命者、景行天皇の皇子なり。

translated_text: He was brave and valiant, and pacified the provinces.
original_text: 其勇武にして、諸国を平定せり。

translated_text: When he went to the eastern conquest, his father the Emperor bestowed upon him a sacred sword.
original_text: 東征の時、父帝、宝剣を賜ふ。

translated_text: This sword was the Kusanagi no Tsurugi. It was taken by Izanagi from the tail of the great serpent.
original_text: 此剣者、天叢雲劒なり。伊奘諾尊、大蛇の尾より取りし者なり。

translated_text: Prince Yamato Takeru used this sword to defeat the rebels and pacify the provinces.
original_text: 倭建命、此剣を以て賊を討ち、諸国を平定せり。

translated_text: Yet when his time of death approached, he lost the sword.
original_text: 然るに死期至りて、剣を失ふ。

translated_text: His spirit transformed into a white bird and flew across the sky.
original_text: 其魂化して白鳥と成り、空を飛ぶ。

translated_text: Amaterasu commanded her grandson Ninigi no Mikoto, saying:
original_text: 天照大御神、天孫瓊瓊杵命に勅して曰く。

translated_text: Japan is the land of divine command. To govern it is the duty of the Imperial Grandson.
original_text: 日本は神勅の国なり。此を治むるは、皇孫の任なり。

translated_text: She bestowed upon him the Three Sacred Treasures and entrusted him with the governance of the land.
original_text: 三種の神器を授け、治天下を託す。

translated_text: The mirror is the spirit of Amaterasu. The sword was obtained by Susanoo from the great serpent. The jewel was given by Toyotama-hime.
original_text: 鏡は天照大御神の魂なり。剣は須佐之男命の大蛇より得たり。玉は豊玉比賣の授けし物なり。

translated_text: These three treasures are the sacred treasures passed down through the imperial line.
original_text: 此三宝は、皇統相承の神器なり。

translated_text: In heaven there are gods, on earth there are gods. In the sea there are gods, on the mountains there are gods.
original_text: 天に神あり、地に神あり。海に神あり、山に神あり。

translated_text: Gods of the land, heavenly gods, the eight million deities!
original_text: 國の神、天津神、八百萬の神々よ。

translated_text: Before these deities, we offer words, present the pure mirror, and raise the white offerings.
original_text: 此の神の御前に、詞を奉り、真澄ます鏡を捧げて、白き大幣を立てて。

translated_text: Heavenly gods, earthly gods, eight million deities! May the land be firm, the people at peace, the five grains abundant, and growth flourish.
original_text: 天津神、國つ神、八百萬の神々よ。國の固め、人の安けく、五穀豐かに、成長ますように。

translated_text: May the Emperor rightly succeed to the heavenly throne and the imperial position.
original_text: よろしく天つ日嗣とし、皇位を継ぎたまふherits。

translated_text: Heavenly gods, earthly gods, eight million deities! We untie the sins of heaven, untie the sins of the earth, untie ten sins, untie a hundred sins, untie a thousand sins, untie ten thousand sins.
original_text: 天津神、國津神、八百萬の神々よ。天つ罪を解き、國つ罪を解き、十の罪を解き、百の罪を解き、千の罪を解き、萬の罪を解き。

translated_text: Shinto is the way of revering the gods who dwell in all things and honoring nature.
original_text: 神道は万物に宿る神を敬い、自然を崇める道なり。

translated_text: Purification is the act of cleansing heart and body. Misogi is the ritual of washing the body with water.
original_text: 清めは心と身を淨める行なり。禊は水にて身を洗ふ儀式なり。

translated_text: The mirror is the dwelling place of the gods. The sacred object of Ise Shrine is the eight-span mirror.
original_text: 鏡は神の依り代なり。伊勢の神宮の神体は、八咫の鏡なり。

translated_text: If one worships with a bright and pure heart, the gods will also illuminate one's heart.
original_text: 明けき心を以て神を祭れば、神も亦、人の心を照し給ふ。

translated_text: The violent god is an enraged deity. The peaceful spirit is a harmonious deity.
original_text: 荒ぶる神は怒れる神なり。和魂は和ぎたる神なり。

translated_text: The gods are the beings who connect heaven and earth, the human world and the divine world.
original_text: 神は天と地の間、人の世と神の世とを繋ぐものなり。

translated_text: Amaterasu commanded: Japan is the land governed by the descendants of the gods.
original_text: 天照大御神勅して曰く、日本は神の孫の治むる国なり。

translated_text: The Land of Luxuriant Reed Plains of a Thousand Autumns of Fine Rice, the land where my descendants shall reign.
original_text: 豊葦原の千五百秋の瑞穂の国は、吾が子孫の王すべき地なり。

translated_text: The descent of the Heavenly Grandchild — this is the divine command to govern this land.
original_text: 天孫の降臨、此の国を治めんとの神勅なり。

translated_text: The imperial line begins with Amaterasu and is an unbroken lineage for ten thousand generations.
original_text: 皇統は天照大御神より始まり、万世一系のものなり。

translated_text: With the Three Sacred Treasures, the imperial succession is maintained.
original_text: 神器三種を以て、皇位を継ぎたまふ。

translated_text: Ise Shrine is the foremost shrine dedicated to Amaterasu.
original_text: 伊勢の神宮は、天照大御神を祀る第一の神社なり。

translated_text: Izumo Taisha is the great shrine dedicated to Okuninushi no Mikoto.
original_text: 出雲大社は、大国主命を祀る大社なり。

translated_text: Mount Fuji is a sacred mountain. Many deities dwell in this holy mountain.
original_text: 富士山は神体山なり。多くの神が宿る聖なる山なり。

translated_text: The shimenawa rope marks the boundary between the sacred and the profane.
original_text: 注連縄は、聖と俗を区別する結界なり。

translated_text: The gohei is an offering presented to the gods — paper attached to a wand.
original_text: 御幣は神に捧げる捧げ物なり。紙を木に付けたる物なり。

translated_text: The omikuji is an oracle. It is the way of knowing the mind of the gods.
original_text: 御神籤は神託なり。神の御心を知る術なり。

translated_text: The purification ritual cleanses impurity. It removes sin and defilement.
original_text: お祓いは穢れを清める儀式なり。罪と穢れを除くものなり。

translated_text: The gods dwell in all things. They dwell in flowers, in trees, in the wind, in water.
original_text: 神は万物に宿る。花に宿り、木に宿り、風に宿り、水に宿る。

translated_text: The eight million deities overflow between heaven and earth.
original_text: 八百萬の神々は、天地の間に溢れ給ふ。

translated_text: The gods are to be feared and revered. Yet the gods are near to human beings.
original_text: 神は畏れ敬べきものなり。然れども、神は人の近くにあり給ふ。

translated_text: When a person's heart is pure, the gods respond and bestow blessings.
original_text: 人の心清ければ、神も亦、之に応じて恵み給ふ。

translated_text: The household deity protects the home. The tutelary deity protects the land.
original_text: 荒神は家を守る神なり。氏神はその土地を守る神なり。

translated_text: Festivals are the communion between gods and humans. They please the gods and bring joy to people.
original_text: 祭りは神と人との交わりなり。神を楽しませ、人も亦、喜ぶ儀式なり。
